title: One fixed UV spectrum fails the full 2023 ASASSN-14ko flare test with 1-percent independent calibration errors
abstract: We test one fixed variable UV spectrum in 25 XMM-Newton OM visits of the 2023 ASASSN-14ko flare. A count-rate relation with a free intercept removes the need to subtract constant host and companion light. With 1-percent independent calibration errors added, the fixed-spectrum fit gives chi-square 50.66 for 23 degrees of freedom. Two time segments improve this by 33.25. No larger improvement occurs in 999 null simulations that repeat the split search. At a matched UVW2 rate, the late fit has 7.96 percent more UVM2 flux. The main flare alone admits a fixed spectrum. The absolute-fit rejection disappears with 2-percent errors; the split-search probability rises to 0.036 at 3 percent. Fast-mode extraction also departs from a fixed spectrum but selects an earlier split. The result constrains a common scalar emission response during the clock-stall era. It does not identify an emission mechanism, measure a new orbital period, or establish a physical transition time. All code, aggregate fits, input hashes and verified-source retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: The two-band rate relation and its time-ordered residuals, with 1-percent independent calibration errors. The shaded gap contains the best searched split.
